_comment: Tao Te Ching 33 and 78 replaced with Waley, closing the textual-identification pass. Criteria applied in order: fidelity, editorial fit, rights - not convenience. Waley clears fidelity cleanly for both, and the book then gets a secondary benefit rather than a manufactured one: one Tao Te Ching translator, one textual voice, three chapters.

entries.match: Nothing under heaven is softer or more yielding than water
entries.translator_or_mediator: Arthur Waley, The Way and Its Power (1934) - NAMED in the manuscript
entries.editorial_status: REPLACED. The previous wording - 'Nothing is softer or more flexible than water, yet nothing can resist it' - was not a translation at all: it appeared only on quote sites with no translator and matched none of the named renderings checked. Waley's first sentence alone carries both halves the passage needs, so the quotation was not enlarged merely because the whole chapter became available.

provenance_history.note: Applied to a circulating compression whose English could not be attributed to any translator; the identification pass established it was not a translation, and the wording was deliberately replaced.

entries.match: To understand others is to have knowledge
entries.translator_or_mediator: Arthur Waley, The Way and Its Power (1934) - NAMED in the manuscript
entries.editorial_status: REPLACED. The previous wording was verbatim in TWO named renderings, Rosenthal (1984) and Cheng Lin, so the wording itself could not tell us whose English the book was printing - and citing 'Tao Te Ching 33' alone while printing somebody's modern English would have concealed the very mediation layer this audit exists to recover. Waley's rendering is more austere than what it replaces; if the Conclusion still works with the actual source, the source earns its place, and if it does not, the quotation is reconsidered rather than Laozi tuned to the chapter.

provenance_history.evidence_location: QUOTATION_PROVENANCE_AUDIT.md (Tao Te Ching 33, demonstrably not Legge)
provenance_history.note: Applied to an English matched by two named renderings and attributable to neither; replaced deliberately rather than attached to a translator by resemblance.
